C / PERSONAL PROJECTS

Last Label / When should learning stop?

Python / small-text / scikit-learn

Annotation cost and predictive performance under noisy labels and biased stop sets

  • Evaluated published SP and PCF stopping rules across 15,360 learning trajectories on six binary tasks.
  • Analyzed paired cost-performance differences, budget fallbacks, noise interactions, and stopping-convention sensitivity.

Loading saved experiment...

LastLabel is my independent study of when a learning system should stop requesting human labels. Building on methods by Dr. Michael Bloodgood and his coauthors, I compared labeling effort with performance on unseen examples across 15,360 training runs. The experiments examine incorrect labels and different ways of checking whether learning has settled. Saving labels can also mean giving up performance, and the best stopping point depends on the task. Study, methods, and full results ↗

SENSORLAB / Learning where to measure

Thermal inference / Experimental design

Simulation guided sensor placement for thermal property estimation.

  • Built a differentiable heat solver to estimate material properties from sparse, noisy measurements.
  • Validated gradients and compared sensor layouts using equal measurement budgets.

SENSORLAB investigates where to measure temperature to estimate how a material conducts heat. I built a differentiable heat solver and checked its gradients against finite differences. I compared adaptive, uniform, and random sensor layouts using equal measurement budgets, evaluating estimation error, uncertainty, and whether the measurements distinguish different material properties. The goal is to guide more informative measurements when testing time and resources are limited.

LUMEN / CPU and GPU path tracer

C++ / CUDA / OpenGL

Path tracing for physically based lighting simulation

  • Built a multithreaded CPU path tracer with BVH traversal, area lights, and multiple importance sampling.
  • Implemented a CUDA wavefront backend and progressive OpenGL viewer.

LUMEN builds images by following simulated light as it bounces around a scene. That produces soft shadows, reflections, and glass effects from the same lighting model. I built CPU and GPU renderers and compared their output and rendering time. The slider uses saved renders, so it responds without a powerful graphics card. Source code and rendering benchmarks ↗
